title: Pontotoc sweet potato station gets $250,000 grant for backup power and new greenhouses
excerpt: After a seven-day outage left staff tending plants around the clock, Mississippi State plans a generator, electrical upgrades and two replacement greenhouses.
locality: Pontotoc Ridge-Flatwoods Branch Experiment Station on Mississippi 15 South in Pontotoc County, Mississippi.

paragraphs.text: A $250,000 federal grant will help put backup power in place and replace two greenhouses at Mississippi State University’s sweet potato research station in Pontotoc County. During last winter’s ice storm, the station was without electricity for seven days and staff kept watch around the clock to save its planting stock.

Growers across the Southeast rely on the station for virus-tested sweet potato planting material. Its lab keeps that stock in temperature-controlled equipment. The new generator and electrical work at the lab and main office will give staff a way to protect it during another outage.

The two replacement greenhouses will have better drainage, extra lighting and shade cloths that adjust automatically. The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture awarded the grant. The Mississippi Agricultural and Forestry Experiment Station is also contributing funds. MSU expects the work to take up to two years.

The Pontotoc Ridge-Flatwoods Branch is at 8320 Highway 15 South. The greenhouse work complements a separate sweet potato storage building under construction there. Together, the facilities will let researchers follow the crop from young plants through storage after harvest.
